entries.name: Bringing it out of storage
entries.description: The other half of a winter prep: what to look at before a vehicle that has sat for months goes back on the road. Most of these happen because it sat rather than because it was driven, which is why an ordinary service checklist misses them. Generic.
entries.author: HomeAutoShop

entries.name: Before hitching up
entries.description: Five minutes in the driveway before towing anything. Short on purpose: a check nobody completes is worse than a shorter one everybody does, and every item here is something that fails at highway speed with a trailer attached. Generic, and a trailer with electric or surge brakes will want items of its own added.
entries.author: HomeAutoShop

entries.name: Roadworthy quick check
entries.description: A ten-minute walk around before a long drive. Deliberately short: a check nobody completes is worse than a shorter one everybody does.
entries.author: HomeAutoShop

entries.name: Four-wheel drive extras
entries.description: The driveline items a two-wheel-drive schedule has no reason to mention: transfer case, front differential, front axle and hubs. Meant to be applied alongside a normal or severe schedule rather than instead of one, since it covers what the others leave out. Generic intervals; check them against your own owner's manual, and shorten all of them if the vehicle sees water, mud or salt, every one of which gets into a transfer case.
entries.author: HomeAutoShop

entries.name: Stored or seasonal vehicle
entries.description: A classic, a convertible, a project, or anything that spends most of the year parked. Deliberately has no distance intervals at all: a vehicle covering four hundred miles a year will never reach a mileage service, while its brake fluid still absorbs water, its tires still age out, and its fuel still goes stale on exactly the same calendar as everybody else's. Generic; check against your owner's manual.
entries.author: HomeAutoShop

entries.name: Towing and heavy hauling
entries.description: For a truck or SUV that tows a trailer, carries a camper, or spends its life loaded. Heat is what shortens these intervals — automatic transmission fluid and differential oil age far faster under load than mileage alone suggests, and brakes do the work of a much heavier vehicle. Generic and conservative; check against your own owner's manual, which will usually have a towing column of its own.
entries.author: HomeAutoShop

entries.name: Trailer
entries.description: A utility, boat, or equipment trailer. No engine, so nothing here is an engine service. What fails on a trailer is bearings, brakes, tires and lights, and it fails at speed with somebody's boat behind it. Distance is towed miles. Generic; check against the axle manufacturer's figures, which are usually stricter than the trailer builder's.
entries.author: HomeAutoShop
